title: KV & Stream saturation mitigation: fallthrough profiles and adaptive connection trimming
creator: Sana Iyer
description: Problem: In high tail load events we observe cascading latency and error amplification from Redis and Kafka leading to SLO breaches for hosted API endpoints. This ticket defines a deployable pattern: per-tenant "fallthrough profiles" that encode graded degradation, an adaptive connection-trimming controller for connection pools, and region-aware fallback policies for streaming reads. Goal is to prevent single dependency saturation from causing global request-level SLO violations while preserving best-effort correctness for critical customers.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON schema for fallthrough profiles and add to config-service (profile includes priorities, acceptable staleness, cache-route, hedging-policy, circuit thresholds)
Implement adaptive connection-trimming controller that actively reduces idle/concurrent connections to Redis/Postgres based on p99 latency and connection queue length
Add region-aware streaming fallback: on Kafka fetch stall, fallback to cached checkpoint or degrade to last-known-consistent read with clear audit logging
New dashboards showing per-tenant induced-degradation rate, SLO impact, and successful auto-recoveries; SLO regressions must be <5% vs baseline during staged chaos tests
Run chaos experiment and show that during injected Redis slowdowns, 95% of requests remain within latency SLO due to fallthrough behavior
tasks: Spec: fallthrough profile schema + UI fields in Console (Sana) - link to confluence
Runtime: connection-trimming controller (Liam) - implement token-bucket eviction and soft-close protocol
Runtime: graded circuit breaker library extension (Anita) - supports soft-trips and probation periods
RD: Kafka consumer fallback adapter (Jorge) - return checkpointed payloads with metadata
E2E: integration tests and chaos pipelines (QA) - resilient failover scenarios
Observability: add per-profile metrics and alerting (Sam) - create dashboards and SLO alerts
decisions: Use a centralized profile stored in config-service to avoid per-host drift; profiles are versioned and can be pinned per-customer
Adaptive trimming will be rate-limited and conservative: start by shedding idle connections then progressive reduction of active concurrent streams
Circuit breaker states extended: CLOSED -> SOFT-OPEN (serve degraded) -> OPEN -> PROBATION; SOFT-OPEN returns cached results or partial responses instead of hard failures
Hedging is region-aware: primary region attempts first, if timeout threshold reached then start parallel hedges to secondary regions up to N hedges where N is profile-controlled
We will favor observable, reversible changes over aggressive hard-fails to reduce customer surprises; admin override in Console required for full hard-fails

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive shedding reduces SLO risk but increases inconsistency and potential data staleness; profiles must balance business-critical read consistency vs latency guarantees
Rollout plan: feature-flagged, start with internal tenants only -> opt-in customers -> 1% canary -> 10% -> full. Monitor degrade-rate and user-facing errors closely.
Testing: include tenant-scoped tests to ensure high-priority tenants are protected from trimming by default. Provide a 'priority=high' profile template that disables non-critical shedding.
Follow-ups: add CLI/Console tooling to simulate profile effects for a tenant and to generate 'what-if' cost/latency estimates
